skill-scaffold-style-neutralskill-scaffolding0 of 0.125 (minor)failThe requirement says that when the skill scaffolds a presentation app, the scaffold must not define default presentation colors, fonts, button styles, borders or CSS theme tokens. The default scaffold breaks this. In scaffold.mjs, `starter` stays true unless `--no-starter` is passed (line 15), and it is passed to `scaffold(plan.appDir, { install, starter })` (line 30). In lib.mjs, `scaffold()` defaults `starter = true` (line 253) and calls `scaffoldIndex(appDir, report, starter)` whenever the index anchor is missing (lines 264-266). That covers every empty or unscaffolded target. `scaffoldIndex` then calls `createPresentation(appDir, &#39;getting-started&#39;, &#39;Getting Started&#39;, report)` when `withStarter` is true (lines 241-245). The body of `createPresentation` walks every file in `PRESENTATION_TEMPLATE_DIR` (which is `templates/presentation`, line 10). It writes each file, rendered, into `src/presentations/getting-started/` (lines 316-321). So the scaffolded app gets talk.css and Talk.tsx. talk.css defines theme tokens (`--ink`, `--muted`, `--gold`, `--line`, `--panel`, `--ok`), a `#0d0c0b` background and an Inter font stack (lines 3-15). It also defines button styles with padding, a 1px border and a 999px radius (lines 38-56), and bordered, rounded entity cards (lines 132-141). Talk.tsx imports &#39;./talk.css&#39; and wraps the presentation in that class (lines 1-11), so the styling is active in the scaffolded output. SKILL.md 77-78 confirms that a fresh scaffold includes this `getting-started` presentation. Judges A and C ruled pass because the bootstrap package.json, vite.config.ts, src/index.css (`body { margin: 0 }`) and the kit are neutral, and A called talk.css presentation-owned and removable. Those facts are accurate, but they do not decide the requirement. The clause covers the scaffold&#39;s default output, and that output includes a starter whose stylesheet defines exactly the forbidden defaults. Saying the folder can be removed later (SKILL.md 77-78) does not stop the scaffold from writing it by default. SKILL.md&#39;s own neutrality claim (line 74) is prose, and the delivered helper behaves otherwise. C cites the integration test, but by Judge B&#39;s account it checks only the kit, package.json, vite.config.ts and index.css, so it never examines the generated starter stylesheet. The bootstrap package.json has no Tailwind, vite.config.ts is plain, the host index.css only sets `body { margin: 0 }`, and the kit ships no CSS. The majority&#39;s reason is that the default scaffold writes a themed starter presentation. The material shows this, and the dissent doesn&#39;t refute it. scaffold.mjs keeps `starter = true` unless --no-starter is passed. In lib.mjs, `scaffold()` defaults `starter = true`, and when the index anchor is missing it calls scaffoldIndex(..., starter), which calls createPresentation(appDir, &#39;getting-started&#39;, ...). That copies templates/presentation into the app, including talk.css. talk.css defines CSS theme tokens (--ink, --muted, --gold, --line, --panel, --ok), a #0d0c0b background, an Inter font stack, bordered pill-shaped button styles and bordered rounded entity cards. I found no import that resolves outside src, no unresolved CSS import, no missing required prop and no mismatched field name. The presentation templates are written to `&lt;appDir&gt;/src/presentations/&lt;slug&gt;/` by `createPresentation` in `lib.mjs`. From there, `Talk.tsx` imports `../../presentation-kit`, which is `src/presentation-kit/index.ts`. `steps/Scene.tsx` sits one level deeper and imports `../../../presentation-kit`, which resolves to the same place. `steps/Scene.tsx` imports `../entities`, `steps/index.ts` imports `./Scene`, and `Talk.tsx` imports `./steps`. All of those files exist in the template. `Talk.tsx` imports `./talk.css`, which is a template file with no `@import` of its own. The registry line that `registerInSource` writes is `import(&#39;./&lt;slug&gt;/Talk&#39;)` inside `src/presentations/index.ts`. That resolves to `src/presentations/&lt;slug&gt;/Talk`, and `Talk` has a default export, matching `PresentationEntry.load`. Props and field names match the kit types: - **`Presentation`:** `Talk.tsx` passes `steps`, `title` and `initialMode`. `PresentationProps` requires only `steps`. - **`Step`:** each entry in `steps/index.ts` supplies `id`, `era`, `title`, `caption`, `Scene`, `payload` and `groupKey`, which is every required field plus the optional `groupKey`. - **`Box` and `Label`:** the scene passes `id`, `x` and `y`, which `NodeProps` requires, plus optional `w`, `h` and `className`. - **`Arrow`:** the scene passes `id`, `from`, `to` and `className`. `ArrowProps` requires only `id`, `from` and `to`. - **`Appear` and `SceneLayer`:** both are given only `children`, which is all they require. - **`Scene`:** it is typed as `SceneProps&lt;ScenePayload&gt;`, matching `Step.Scene`. Unused imports are not a problem under `noUnusedLocals`, because every import in the templates is used. The inspect template is `scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs`, and the scaffold copies the whole `scripts/` tree, including `lib/`. Its relative imports are `./lib/diagnostics.mjs`, `./lib/preview.mjs`, `./lib/settle.mjs` and `./lib/snapshot.mjs`. All four exist in the bootstrap template. The named imports match the actual exports: - **`diagnostics.mjs`:** `ATTRIBUTION_HINT`, `findAttributionIssues`, `findClippedChrome`, `findIndistinctActive`, `findOverlaps`, `findSmallText` and `SMALL_TEXT_MIN_PX`. - **`preview.mjs`:** `launchBrowser`, `sleep`, `startPreview` and `waitForStepIndex`. - **`settle.mjs`:** `settleThenCapture`. - **`snapshot.mjs`:** `collectSnapshot`. `diagnostics.mjs` imports nothing, and `MIN_RENDERED_TEXT_PX` is defined inside it. `preview.mjs` imports `playwright` and `vite`, and both are in the bootstrap `package.json` devDependencies. The `npm run inspect` script points at `scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs`. The first part is met. The bootstrap package.json lists no Tailwind or other styling framework, and the host index.css only resets the body margin. The second part is not met. scaffold() in lib.mjs defaults to starter = true, and scaffold.mjs keeps that default unless the caller passes --no-starter. When the starter is on, scaffoldIndex() calls createPresentation() for &#39;getting-started&#39;, which copies every file in templates/presentation into the new app. That includes talk.css, which Talk.tsx imports. talk.css defines CSS custom-property tokens (--ink, --muted, --gold, --line, --panel, --ok), a #0d0c0b background, an Inter font stack, button colors and backgrounds, pill borders on the navigation buttons, and bordered, rounded .entity cards. So the default scaffold output contains default presentation colors, fonts, button styles, borders and theme tokens. SKILL.md lines 77-78 confirm that a fresh scaffold includes this starter. Judge B&#39;s reason is borne out by this source, and it decides the requirement, so I rule B&#39;s fail. Judges A and C are correct that the bootstrap template&#39;s package.json, vite.config.ts, index.css and kit are free of styling, but that only proves the framework-neutral part. A argues the starter is presentation-owned and removable. The requirement, however, is about what the scaffold defines, not where the styling lives: the scaffold still writes the themed talk.css by default, and the user would have to remove it. C&#39;s reliance on the integration test does not decide it either. The &#39;imposes no styling framework&#39; test checks only the kit, package.json, vite.config.ts and index.css. The default scaffold breaks this. In scaffold.mjs, `starter` stays true unless `--no-starter` is passed (line 15), and it is passed to `scaffold(plan.appDir, { install, starter })` (line 30). In lib.mjs, `scaffold()` defaults `starter = true` (line 253) and calls `scaffoldIndex(appDir, report, starter)` whenever the index anchor is missing (lines 264-266). That covers every empty or unscaffolded target. `scaffoldIndex` then calls `createPresentation(appDir, &#39;getting-started&#39;, &#39;Getting Started&#39;, report)` when `withStarter` is true (lines 241-245). The body of `createPresentation` walks every file in `PRESENTATION_TEMPLATE_DIR` (which is `templates/presentation`, line 10). It writes each file, rendered, into `src/presentations/getting-started/` (lines 316-321). So the scaffolded app gets talk.css and Talk.tsx. talk.css defines theme tokens (`--ink`, `--muted`, `--gold`, `--line`, `--panel`, `--ok`), a `#0d0c0b` background and an Inter font stack (lines 3-15). It also defines button styles with padding, a 1px border and a 999px radius (lines 38-56), and bordered, rounded entity cards (lines 132-141). Talk.tsx imports &#39;./talk.css&#39; and wraps the presentation in that class (lines 1-11), so the styling is active in the scaffolded output. SKILL.md 77-78 confirms that a fresh scaffold includes this `getting-started` presentation. Judges A and C ruled pass because the bootstrap package.json, vite.config.ts, src/index.css (`body { margin: 0 }`) and the kit are neutral, and A called talk.css presentation-owned and removable. Those facts are accurate, but they do not decide the requirement. The clause covers the scaffold&#39;s default output, and that output includes a starter whose stylesheet defines exactly the forbidden defaults. Saying the folder can be removed later (SKILL.md 77-78) does not stop the scaffold from writing it by default. SKILL.md&#39;s own neutrality claim (line 74) is prose, and the delivered helper behaves otherwise. C cites the integration test, but by Judge B&#39;s account it checks only the kit, package.json, vite.config.ts and index.css, so it never examines the generated starter stylesheet. rule with panels A and B. All three clauses, as the review guidance defines them, are met for every public primitive exported from src/presentation-kit/index.ts. 1. **Typed props, not an untyped bag.** Each primitive has explicit typed props: NodeProps, BoxProps, SymbolChipProps, ArrowProps, or inline typed props for Appear and SceneLayer. None uses Record&lt;string, unknown&gt; or a similar bag. 2. **Identity hooks cannot be overridden.** No primitive spreads caller props onto the motion or DOM element. layoutId, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-id are set as fixed values on the rendered element, so callers cannot override them. 3. **Kit-only props stay off the DOM.** x, y, w and h only feed boxStyle. Icon is rendered as a child. variant becomes data-presentation-variant. label becomes aria-label/role. from, to, bend and both only compute the path. delay only drives the animation. Panel C fails the primitives because they use standalone kit interfaces instead of the rendered element&#39;s props. The material does show that, but it does not decide this criterion. The requirement frames the typing clause as a contrast with &quot;an untyped bag such as Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;&quot;. The guidance fails a primitive only for an untyped bag, for spreading caller props after its identity hooks, or for forwarding a kit-only prop. It also says typed primitives that apply identity hooks after caller props and strip kit-only props pass. None of the delivered test files drives a browser itself. - tests/e2e/verify.test.ts and tests/integration/inspect.test.ts run `npm run verify` or the inspect script as child processes through runAsync. runAsync waits for the child&#39;s close event. The tests then assert on the exit status, the output and report.json, which are final results rather than live page state, so no fixed sleep comes before those assertions. - The tests contain no page access, waitForTimeout or sleep. The only test-file timer, the fixed setTimeout in src/presentation-kit/nodes/nodes.test.tsx, is in a jsdom unit test (vitest.config.ts sets environment: &#39;jsdom&#39;), not a browser test. Its final assertion is a polling waitFor. - Inside the browser the tests launch, verify confirms each step with waitForStepIndex. That is Playwright&#39;s polling page.waitForFunction on data-step-index, with a timeout, so the step assertion waits on observable state. Panel C fails the criterion because verify.mjs sleeps SETTLE_MS before reading title and caption, and inspect waits a fixed settle interval before capturing. That material is accurate but does not decide the requirement. Those are the delivered verify and inspect tools, which are scored under the verification-tooling criteria, not browser-driving test code. Verify waits for the step index by polling before the sleep, so the sleep is an extra settle delay, which the guidance lists as validator noise. The inspect settle interval is the helper&#39;s capture feature, not a wait before an assertion on the step.","evidence":["tests/helpers.ts runAsync spawns a child process and resolves only on its &#39;close&#39; event with status and output. All three clauses, as the review guidance defines them, are met for every public primitive exported from src/presentation-kit/index.ts. 1. **Typed props, not an untyped bag.** Each primitive has explicit typed props: NodeProps, BoxProps, SymbolChipProps, ArrowProps, or inline typed props for Appear and SceneLayer. None uses Record&lt;string, unknown&gt; or a similar bag. 2. **Identity hooks cannot be overridden.** No primitive spreads caller props onto the motion or DOM element. layoutId, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-id are set as fixed values on the rendered element, so callers cannot override them. 3. **Kit-only props stay off the DOM.** x, y, w and h only feed boxStyle. Icon is rendered as a child. variant becomes data-presentation-variant. label becomes aria-label/role. from, to, bend and both only compute the path. delay only drives the animation. Panel C fails the primitives because they use standalone kit interfaces instead of the rendered element&#39;s props. The material does show that, but it does not decide this criterion. The requirement frames the typing clause as a contrast with &quot;an untyped bag such as Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;&quot;. The guidance fails a primitive only for an untyped bag, for spreading caller props after its identity hooks, or for forwarding a kit-only prop. It also says typed primitives that apply identity hooks after caller props and strip kit-only props pass. No delivered browser-driving test sleeps for a fixed time. Which tests touch a browser: vitest.integration.config.ts:8 limits browser and filesystem tests to tests/integration/**/*.test.ts and tests/e2e/**/*.test.ts. Per the file list, those are exactly three files: tests/e2e/verify.test.ts, tests/integration/inspect.test.ts and tests/integration/bootstrap.test.ts. All three are quoted in full. Every other test runs under vitest.config.ts with environment &#39;jsdom&#39; (line 7), so none of them drives a browser. What the browser tests do: none of the three files opens a Playwright page or calls waitForTimeout, a sleep, or a timed setTimeout. Each one spawns the project scripts through runAsync or run. runAsync resolves only on the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event (tests/helpers.ts:60), and the tests assert only after that, on exit status, output and report.json. The setTimeout at verify.test.ts:96 is a 0 ms delay inside text injected into the fixture to throw an uncaught error. It is a fault-injection payload, not a wait in the test. Where the scripts step the deck, they wait on observable state. After each ArrowRight, verify.mjs:71-76 calls waitForStepIndex. preview.mjs:58-63 implements that as page.waitForFunction, polling until data-step-index equals the target, with a timeout. The scripts read titles and captions only after that. Judge C&#39;s fail does not decide the criterion. The sleep(SETTLE_MS) at verify.mjs:78 is in the verification script, not in a test. It runs after the waitForStepIndex poll has already confirmed the step, so it does not replace a state wait. The guidance also lists longer fixed settle delays as validator noise. INT-002&#39;s SETTLE_MS of 1300 (inspect.test.ts:6, 110, 138) is a CLI argument passed to the inspect tool, and the test then asserts on the recorded capturedAfterMs. The test itself never sleeps. Judges A and B (pass) are borne out. The only fixed timer in the test tree is at nodes.test.tsx:93. SymbolChip takes SymbolChipProps and Arrow takes ArrowProps, both standalone interfaces. Appear and SceneLayer take inline object types. None of these types is built from the props of the rendered element (a motion.div, motion.span, motion.svg or div). Avoiding Record&lt;string, unknown&gt; does not make a type the rendered element&#39;s props. The guidance says typed primitives that &quot;apply identity hooks after caller props and strip kit-only props pass&quot;. That describes primitives that accept and forward the element&#39;s caller props. These primitives accept none, so that pass case does not apply here. span audit's stated contradiction was confirmed by an independent check: The claim does not hold, because the first clause of the requirement is unmet. The requirement passes primitives only when &quot;they type their props as the rendered element&#39;s props rather than an untyped bag&quot;. The quoted lines show that none of the primitives does this. Box, Label, Frame and Emphasis take NodeProps, a standalone kit interface with only id, x, y, w, h, className, style and children. SymbolChip takes SymbolChipProps and Arrow takes ArrowProps, both standalone interfaces. Appear and SceneLayer take inline object types. None of these types is built from the props of the rendered element (a motion.div, motion.span, motion.svg or div). Avoiding Record&lt;string, unknown&gt; does not make a type the rendered element&#39;s props. The guidance says typed primitives that &quot;apply identity hooks after caller props and strip kit-only props pass&quot;. That describes primitives that accept and forward the element&#39;s caller props. These primitives accept none, so that pass case does not apply here. The quoted material shows clauses two and three are met: there is no spread of caller props onto the element, and the kit-only props do not reach the DOM. The material also shows the typing clause is not met, so the claimed pass is contradicted. | The auditor&#39;s point holds. The requirement sets out the complete pass condition, and its first clause says the primitives must &quot;type their props as the rendered element&#39;s props rather than an untyped bag&quot;. That clause names a specific type: the props of the rendered element. Having some typed interface is not enough. The material shows that no public primitive meets it. Box, Label, Frame and Emphasis take NodeProps or an extension of it. NodeProps is a standalone kit interface with only id, x, y, w, h, className, style and children, and nothing in it derives from the props of motion.div or motion.span. ArrowProps is a standalone interface for a component that renders a motion.svg. Appear and SceneLayer take inline object types with only children, delay, className and style. The pass verdict relied on the guidance&#39;s list of failure examples, but that list illustrates failures and does not replace the requirement&#39;s positive condition. The guidance&#39;s pass case also describes primitives that apply identity hooks after caller props, which means primitives that accept and forward element props. These primitives forward none. Clauses two and three are met, since nothing is spread onto the element and kit-only props stay off the DOM. dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[],"scene-kit":[],"presentation-skill":[],"verification-tooling":[],"engineering-quality":[{"id":"engineering-typed-kit-primitives","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"The fail verdict rests only on the first clause: it says the props are a custom NodeProps interface rather than the rendered element&#39;s props. The requirement states that clause as a contrast with &quot;an untyped bag such as Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;&quot;. The review guidance fails a primitive only when it uses such an untyped bag, spreads caller props after its identity hooks, or forwards a kit-only prop to the DOM. The guidance also says &quot;Typed primitives that apply identity hooks after caller props and strip kit-only props pass.&quot; The material shows explicitly typed interfaces (NodeProps, BoxProps, SymbolChipProps, ArrowProps, and inline typed props for Appear and SceneLayer), not an untyped bag. No primitive spreads caller props onto the motion or DOM element. The layoutId, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-id are set as fixed values, so a caller cannot override them. Kit-only props stay off the DOM: Icon is rendered as a child, variant maps to data-presentation-variant, label maps to aria-label/role, x/y/w/h feed boxStyle, and from/to/bend/both and delay are consumed internally. All three clauses, read with the guidance, are met, so the fail is defeated.","evidence":["src/presentation-kit/nodes/shared.ts defines `export interface NodeProps { id: string; x: number; y: number; w?: number; h?: number; className?: string; style?: CSSProperties; children?: ReactNode }`…","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx destructures `{ id, Icon, variant, className, children, ...rest }` and passes `rest` only to `boxStyle({ id, ...rest })`. The motion.div sets layoutId={id}, data-pr…","Label.tsx, Frame.tsx and Emphasis.tsx follow the same pattern: they spread no caller props and set the hooks as fixed values.","SymbolChip.tsx uses `label` only for `aria-label={label}` and `role`. Icon is rendered as a child element.","Arrow.tsx consumes from/to/bend/both internally to build the path. Its motion.svg sets layoutId={id} and data-presentation-id={id} as fixed values; only `style` is spread inside the style object.","Appear.tsx and SceneLayer.tsx use inline typed prop objects and set data-presentation-appear and data-presentation-layer as fixed values, with no caller spread."],"citations":["src/presentation-kit/nodes/shared.ts","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Label.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Frame.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Emphasis.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/SymbolChip.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Arrow.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Appear.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/SceneLayer.tsx"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":1,"sample":2},{"id":"engineering-diagnostics-cover-presentation","classification":"contradicted","rationale":"The criterion fails a helper that runs its diagnostics on only one step, such as only the final step, instead of on every captured step. The auditor&#39;s point is true but narrow: the attribution check is guarded by i === 0, so only step 1 checks the attribution link, which belongs to the presentation as a whole.
